title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 693-695): for each i in a finite index set I there is a group G_i (abstractly isomorphic to a fixed G). Each G_i contains a common normal subgroup 𝔊 with quotient γ_i = G_i/𝔊. These quotients have been identified, via data N_i ⊃ SN_i, with γ_i = N_i/SN_i (diagram (15)). A transitive system of isomorphisms among the γ_i has already been chosen, so all γ_i are identified with one group γ (17)-(18). The problem is to describe, in another form, the extra datum needed to reconstitute the global situation (11): a transitive system of isomorphisms u_ij : G_j → G_i that is the identity on 𝔊 and compatible with the given identifications of the γ_i.

Construction (19). Form the fibre product 𝒢 = ∏_{i∈I, γ} G_i of the G_i over γ. The marginal note records that 𝒢 is an extension 1 → 𝔊^I → 𝒢 → γ → 1.

Claim (20). Such systems u_ij correspond bijectively to subgroups G ⊂ 𝒢 satisfying:
- (a) G ∩ 𝔊^I = δ(𝔊), the diagonal;
- (b) G → γ is surjective.

Reformulation. Starting from (13) and the identification of the γ_i, one has canonically built an extension 𝒢 of γ by 𝔊^I. The supplementary structure (M) is a 'restriction' (reduction) of this extension to an extension of γ by the diagonal subgroup δ(𝔊) ≅ 𝔊. G is then a copy of the global group, sitting in 𝒢 as the common 'graph' of the identifications.

Proof check.
- (⇒) Given u_ij, put G = {(u_{i i0}(g))_i : g ∈ G_{i0}}. It lies in 𝒢 by compatibility over γ. It meets 𝔊^I in the diagonal because the u_ij are the identity on 𝔊. It surjects onto γ.
- (⇐) Given G, each projection p_i : G → G_i is injective: an element of the kernel maps to 1 in γ, so it lies in G ∩ 𝔊^I = δ(𝔊), and its i-th component is 1, so it is trivial.
- Each p_i is surjective: lift the image of g in γ to some x ∈ G by (b). Then x_i^{-1}g ∈ 𝔊, and x·δ(x_i^{-1}g) ∈ G has i-th component g.
- Hence u_ij = p_i p_j^{-1} is transitive, is the identity on 𝔊 (diagonal), and is compatible over γ. The two constructions are mutually inverse.

This is the last page of the dossier; the thread stops here.
errors: No mathematical error. The argument implicitly needs 𝔊 normal in each G_i with G_i/𝔊 ≅ γ; this is given by (18).

Not stated: the set of such data is either empty or a torsor. Two choices differ by automorphisms of G_i trivial on 𝔊 and on γ, i.e. by crossed homomorphisms γ → Z(𝔊). Hence existence and uniqueness questions are governed by Z(𝔊) and the classes of the extensions. The page does not address existence.

ideas.what: Fibre product of the G_i over the common quotient γ, viewed as an extension of γ by 𝔊^I

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but routine group-theoretic reformulation (graph of isomorphisms inside a fibre product over the common quotient), part of bookkeeping for reconstituting a global Galois-type situation from local data. It is the last page of the file and leaves the thread open, but with no identifiable new result or connection.
